∫ 2·asin(x) dx = 2·∫ asin(x) dx

Using integration by parts with u = asin(x), dv = dx:

∫ asin(x) dx = x·asin(x) − ∫ x·(1/√(1−x²)) dx

Now evaluate ∫ x/√(1−x²) dx:

Let w = 1−x², then dw = −2x dx, so dx = −dw/(2x). Then:

∫ x/√(1−x²) dx = −(1/2) ∫ dw/√w = −√(1−x²)

Therefore:

∫ asin(x) dx = x·asin(x) − (−√(1−x²)) = x·asin(x) + √(1−x²)

Multiplying by 2:

∫ 2·asin(x) dx = 2·x·asin(x) + 2·√(1−x²) + C

<answer>2*x*asin(x)+2*sqrt(1-x**2)+C</answer>
